title: What Are Stock Perpetuals? Binance Adds ABBV and EQT - Coin Gabbar
content:
So What Exactly Are Stock Perpetuals in Simple Words on Binance? Stock perpetuals are contracts that follow a company’s share price with no expiry date. A trader picks a direction, and the contract gains or loses as the price moves. The idea comes from how perpetual contracts work in crypto; only the price now belongs to a listed company. Binance TradFi perpetuals tied to shares went live on October 26, 2026, opening a new route for stock trading on Binance. The catch is what a trader does not get: no share in the account, no vote at the company meeting, and no ownership. The contract only tracks a price. Pick long if the price may rise, or short if it may fall. Pay or receive funding while the position stays open. Traditional futures on regulated futures exchanges settle and close on a set date. A perpetual has no scheduled expiry, so a position stays open while margin lasts. Stock perpetuals are stock derivatives, so holding one gives no ownership or voting rights. On October 26, 2026, Binance listed four TradFi perpetuals (TradFi means traditional finance): EIDOUSDT, EQTUSDT, STMUSDT, and ABBVUSDT. This article covers the ABBVUSDT and EQTUSDT contracts, tied to AbbVie and EQT Corporation. The figures below come from the official Binance listing announcement, which describes them as USDT-priced and USDT-settled. EQT Corporation is a US natural gas producer, and AbbVie is a pharmaceutical company. Binance can change leverage, margin rules, and funding settings later, and it says the products may not be available in every region. US shares don’t trade nonstop, but the contracts do, so these stock-linked perpetual contracts need their own pricing method. Three prices matter: Index price: the reference price for the underlying share. Mark price: the price Binance uses for unrealized profit, loss, and liquidation. Contract price: where the perpetual itself trades. It can differ from both of the others, especially outside regular stock-market hours. In regular hours, the index uses prices from data vendors. On weekends, holidays, and maintenance breaks, equity perpetual futures switch to an order-book mode built from the contract’s own trading and smoothed over time, effective May 16, 2026. Under Binance’s TradFi pricing rules, the mark price must stay within 5% of the index on trading days and 3% on weekends and holidays, though Binance can update those limits. Binance also moved the moving average in its mark price formula to a one-minute basis on August 31, 2026, per Binance’s mark price update. In plain words, a Saturday price comes from traders on the contract, not the share market, and it can sit away from Monday’s open. Funding rates are payments between long and short traders. They help keep a perpetual contract’s price aligned with its reference index. A traditional futures contract ends on a set date, but a perpetual never expires. You can hold it for as long as you want, as long as your margin stays safe. Funding can encourage the two prices to meet, but it does not guarantee an exact match. A positive rate usually means long positions pay shorts. Binance-lists a ±2% cap per settlement every eight hours. At that extreme, a 1,000 USDT position implies a 20 USDT payment, though real rates can be far lower. Small rates still add up over days, as these perpetual position costs show. Binance also has a dividend-adjustment mechanism for equity perpetuals. Around the ex-dividend date, a one-time special funding settlement moves money from short holders to long holders to offset the price drop on the shares. For US equities, it begins the calendar day before the ex-dividend date, and the usual funding cap does not apply, so the payment can exceed 2%. The exact treatment depends on Binance’s current rules. Leverage lets you hold a position bigger than the margin you put up. Say you put in 1,000 USDT at 20x. You control 20,000 USDT, so a 5% move against you wipes out the whole margin before fees. Liquidation, which is the forced closing of your position, can happen even sooner because of maintenance margin and platform rules. Binance-says a sharp move against you can wipe out your full margin balance. Leveraged stock trades give you very little room to slip, as these leverage trading risks make clear. Cross margin can put more of your balance behind a single position, while isolated margin caps the margin assigned to that one position. This comparison of cross versus isolated margin explains the difference. Tokenized equity rights depend on the issuer’s legal and custody setup, as a look at tokenized equity products shows. Stock perpetual risks start with leverage. Lower leverage does not remove liquidation risk, since position size, maintenance margin, fees, price gaps, and platform rules all affect losses. Most traders lose positions to the same few errors, and these ways to avoid liquidation show how to steer clear of them. Platforms also calculate it differently, as this note on how liquidation risk differs by exchange shows. Binance has confirmed the launch times, the underlying shares, USDT pricing and settlement, leverage, funding, and trading hours. We did not look into early trading volume, spreads, or order book depth for Binance-stock perpetuals as of October 29, 2026, so you won’t find those numbers here. Thin liquidity and how closely the price follows the stock near the market open are still the main unknowns. With these new contracts, you can trade the price of AbbVie and EQT on Binance-without buying the actual shares. The pairs are ABBVUSDT and EQTUSDT. They trade round the clock, and everything is settled in USDT. Leverage goes up to 20x. Two things need your attention. The first is pricing when the stock market is closed. The contract keeps moving even when the real stock doesn’t, and many traders miss this. The second is leverage. At 20x, a small move against you can wipe out your position very fast. So before you open any trade, check the live contract specs, the funding rate, and your liquidation price. title: Buy, Hold or Sell ABBV Stock? Key Tips Ahead of Q3 Earnings - TradingView
content: AbbVie ABBV is set to report third-quarter 2026 earnings on Oct. 30, before the opening bell. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the to-be-reported quarter’s sales is pinned at $17.37 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) are estimated at $3.77. Both metrics indicate an increase from the year-ago period. Over the past 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 EPS has declined from $14.05 to $13.95, while the 2027 estimate has fallen from $16.15 to $16.05. The near-term decline is primarily attributed to the impact of acquired IPR&D and milestone expenses totaling $216 million, which the company expects to have been recorded in the quarter, as noted in an SEC filing released earlier this month. AbbVie’s performance has been impressive, with its earnings exceeding expectations in each of the trailing four quarters. It has delivered a trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise of 2.10%. In the last reported quarter, the pharma giant delivered an earnings surprise of 0.27%. Per our proven model, companies with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) have a good chance of delivering an earnings beat. This is not the case here. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they’re reported with our Earnings ESP Filter. AbbVie currently has an Earnings ESP of -0.33% and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here. For the third quarter of 2026, AbbVie expects adjusted earnings to be in the range of $3.73-$3.77 per share. The company expects net revenues of approximately $17.2 billion. Currency is expected to have an unfavorable impact of around 0.4% on sales. AbbVie’s top-line growth in the third quarter is likely to have been driven by higher sales of immunology drugs Skyrizi and Rinvoq. Strong volume growth and market share gains across approved indications have been driving sales of both drugs. During the third quarter, Rinvoq’s label was expanded in the EU across three indications — vitiligo, alopecia areata and active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis. This expansion might have further boosted sales in the third quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Skyrizi sales is pegged at $5.72 billion, while the same for Rinvoq is pinned at $2.73 billion. Sales of the company’s flagship drug Humira are likely to have continued their downward trend due to biosimilar erosion. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the drug’s sales is pegged at $695 million. Within AbbVie’s oncology franchise, sales of J&J JNJ-partnered Imbruvica are expected to continue their downward trajectory, reflecting intensifying competition from newer oral therapies. The decline is likely to have accelerated in the to-be-reported quarter, as IRA-driven pricing changes that took effect at the beginning of the year are expected to have put additional pressure on sales. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Imbruvica sales is pegged at approximately $530 million. In contrast, sales of Roche RHHBY-partnered Venclexta are expected to have risen during the to-be-reported quarter, driven by sustained demand in the chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), particularly due to its use in combination with BTK inhibitors. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Venclexta sales is pegged at $793 million. Overall, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for oncology revenues is pegged at $1.68 billion, indicating relatively flat year over year. While the anticipated weakness in Imbruvica sales is expected to weigh on the franchise’s performance, growth in Venclexta and contributions from AbbVie’s newer oncology products are likely to offset this pressure. AbbVie’s neuroscience franchise has delivered strong growth in recent quarters, a trend that is expected to have continued in the to-be-reported quarter. Growth is likely to have been driven by higher sales of Botox Therapeutic, the depression drug Vraylar and the migraine treatments — Ubrelvy and Qulipta. The Parkinson’s disease drug Vyalev is also expected to have contributed to the franchise’s performance during the quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for neuroscience product sales is pinned at approximately $3.29 billion. In the aesthetics franchise, sales are expected to have shown signs of recovery following sluggish performance in recent quarters, primarily due to softness in Botox Cosmetic and Juvederm filler sales. The anticipated improvement is likely to have been supported by stabilizing demand in the U.S. facial injectable market and easing macroeconomic pressures, which may have helped improve consumer sentiment. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for aesthetics product sales is pegged at $1.20 billion, indicating relatively flat year-over-year. Nonetheless, a single quarter’s results are not so important for long-term investors. Let us delve deeper to understand whether to buy, sell or hold the stock at present. Year to date, shares of the company have risen 25.5% compared with the industry’s 17.2% growth. From a valuation standpoint, AbbVie is trading at a discount to the industry. Based on the price/earnings (P/E) ratio, the shares currently trade at 18.29 times forward earnings, lower than the industry’s 19.02 times. Yet, compared to some of its peers like Pfizer PFE and Sanofi, the stock is trading at a premium. AbbVie has navigated Humira’s biosimilar erosion relatively well, with Skyrizi and Rinvoq emerging as its primary growth drivers. Strong demand, market-share gains and label expansions across existing and newer indications have helped the company offset declining Humira sales and strengthen its position in the immunology market. However, competition is intensifying, with J&J’s newly approved oral immunology drug Icotyde potentially posing a longer-term threat to Skyrizi if its use expands into additional indications. The growing neuroscience franchise, driven by Botox Therapeutic, Vraylar and migraine drugs, along with an expanding oncology portfolio, also supports its long-term growth prospects. However, declining Imbruvica sales amid intensifying competition and continued weakness in the aesthetics business remain key headwinds. Meanwhile, AbbVie’s aggressive business development strategy is strengthening its long-term growth prospects but weighing on near-term earnings. The company recently completed its $10.9 billion acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics, further expanding its immunology pipeline. However, the deal is expected to have diluted adjusted EPS by 14 cents in 2026 and approximately 46 cents in 2027, with accretion anticipated beginning in 2032. Additionally, $216 million in acquired IPR&D and milestone expenses is expected to have reduced third-quarter adjusted EPS by $0.11. These costs have contributed to downward revisions in earnings estimates, adding to near-term profitability concerns. While AbbVie’s core growth drivers and pipeline investments support its longer-term outlook, elevated expenses, declining near-term earnings estimates and intensifying competition warrant caution. The company must demonstrate that its investments can translate into sustainable earnings growth to restore near-term investor confidence. Given AbbVie’s Zacks Rank #4, negative Earnings ESP and recent downward revisions in earnings estimates, short-term investors may consider exiting ABBV stock, as near-term earnings uncertainty could limit further upside. However, long-term investors may choose to stay invested, as continued growth in Skyrizi, Rinvoq and other key therapies, along with an expanding pipeline, supports the company’s long-term growth prospects.
